'''Soren Løvtrup''' (1922–2002) was a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Embryology|embryologist]] and [[history of science|historian of science]] in the Department of [[physiology|Animal Physiology]] at the [[Umeå University]], [[Sweden]]. Løvtrup was known for his [[Saltation (biology)#Macromutation theory|macromutation theory]] of evolution, which was in opposition to traditional [[neo-Darwinism]]. In 1987, Løvtrup published his controversial book ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth'' which challenged [[Charles Darwin]]'s role as the intellectual founder of evolutionary theory and accused [[Charles Darwin|Darwin]] of [[plagiarism]].<ref>Vergata, Antonello La. (1989). ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth by Soren Løvtrup''. ''History and Philosophy of the Life Sciences''. Vol. 11, No. 2, pp. 358-360.</ref>

==Career==
Løvtrup was born in [[Copenhagen]]. In 1945, he enrolled at [[University of Copenhagen]], where he obtained a master's degree in [[biochemistry]]. He worked at [[Carlsberg Laboratory]], until 1953 when he received a PhD in [[embryology]]. He also worked at [[University of Gothenburg]]. From 1965, he worked at [[Umeå University]] in Sweden as a professor of animal [[physiology]].

==Research==

=== ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth'' ===

Løvtrup is best known for his book ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth'' (1987).<ref>Vergata, Antonello La. (1989). ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth by Soren Løvtrup''. ''History and Philosophy of the Life Sciences''. Vol. 11, No. 2, pp. 358-360.</ref> In this controversial work, he claimed that [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] was the real founder of evolution and that [[natural selection]] was discovered by [[Erasmus Darwin]], [[Patrick Matthew]] and other naturalists before [[Charles Darwin]]. The book supports the ideas of early evolutionary thinkers such as [[Karl Ernst von Baer]], [[Étienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire]] and [[St. George Jackson Mivart]].<ref name="Thomson 1988">Thomson, Keith Stewart. (1988). ''Darwinism: Refutation of a Myth by Søren Løvtrup''. ''[[American Scientist]]''. Vol. 76, No. 4. pp. 394-395.</ref><ref>Montgomery, William. (1989). ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth by Søren Løvtrup; Darwin and the Emergence of Evolutionary Theories of Mind and Behavior by Robert J. Richards''. ''[[Victorian Studies]]''. Vol. 32, No. 3. pp. 444-445.</ref><ref name="Smith 1989">Smith, Hobart M. (1989). ''The Myth is Not Evolution. Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth by Soren Lovtrup''. ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]''. Vol. 43, No. 3. pp. 699-700.</ref> He was a critic of [[gradualism]] and the [[punctuated equilibrium]] theory of evolution.<ref>Lambert, David. (1988). ''Neo-Darwinism: An Emperor With No Clothes''. ''[[New Scientist]]''. 15, October. p. 66</ref>

Løvtrup argued against the [[Point mutation|micromutation]] theory of the [[modern synthesis (20th century)|modern evolutionary synthesis]] and promoted his own theory of macromutation ([[Saltationism|saltational evolution]]). Biologist [[Bruce Wallace (geneticist)|Bruce Wallace]] gave the book a mixed review, stating that Løvtrup was advocating a minority position in evolutionary biology and he "underestimates existing genetic variation, consequently, he favors evolutionary events that occur rarely even on a geologic time scale."<ref>Wallace, Bruce. (1988). ''Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth by Søren Løvtrup''. ''[[The Quarterly Review of Biology]]''. Vol. 63, No. 2, pp. 214-215.</ref>

Herpetologist [[Hobart Muir Smith]] wrote that the book with its sensationalist title would be highjacked by [[Creationism|creationists]] but it is not against the [[Evolution as fact and theory|fact of evolution]], only against the Darwinian interpretation. Smith concluded "Certainly the book will strike many as controversial, but Løvtrup has given the world a truly epochal, introspective analysis of inestimable potential value."<ref name="Smith 1989"/>

Science historian [[Keith Stewart Thomson]] gave the book a negative review commenting "Many of the sacred cows that Løvtrup wants to slaughter are either long since dead or merely made of straw. It is tedious to constantly to see Darwin and his followers taken to task for failing to be as smart as we are now."<ref name="Thomson 1988"/>

The book was criticized for providing no solid evidence for macromutations, Løvtrup only cited two alleged cases in his book.<ref>Dohle, W. (1988). ''Søren Løvtrup, 1987. Darwinism: The Refutation of a Myth''. ''[[Journal of Evolutionary Biology]]'' 1: 283-285.</ref>

=== Other works ===

Løvtrup's book ''Epigenetics'' (1974) was a work on [[theoretical biology]] which attempted to present a unifying theory of [[Epigenesis (biology)|epigenesis]].<ref>Wiley, E. O. (1977). ''Epigenetics, A Treatise on Theoretical Biology by Soren Lovtrup''. ''[[Systematic Zoology]]''. Vol. 26, No. 2. pp. 238-243.</ref> Biologist [[Clifford Grobstein]] wrote that the book was a mixture of ideas, "sometimes illuminating, sometimes naïve, sometimes superficial, sometimes sophisticated, sometimes enormously detailed."<ref>Grobstein, Clifford. (1975). ''Epigenetics: A Treatise on Theoretical Biology by Soren Lovtrup''. ''[[The Quarterly Review of Biology]]''. Vol. 50, No. 4, p. 439.</ref>

He contributed a paper on his alternative evolutionary views to the book ''Alternative Life-History Styles of Animals'' (1990).<ref>Kaplan, Robert H. (1990). ''Alternative Life-History Styles of Animals by Michael N. Bruton''. ''[[Copeia]]''. Vol. 1990, No. 1, pp. 248-250.</ref>

== Personal life ==
He married [[Ebba Lund]], (a [[Danish resistance movement|Danish Resistance fighter]] and later a microbiologist and chemical engineer) in 1944 and they had three children Vita (1945), Susanne (1948) and Anders (1951) before divorcing in 1959.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Hansen|first=Mogen|date=2003-05-15|title=Dansk Kvindebiografisk Leksikon - Ebba Lund|url=https://www.kvinfo.dk/side/597/bio/1820/origin/170/|access-date=2020-03-02|website=www.kvinfo.dk}}</ref>
